aspects.conjunction:
Two parts of you occupying the same ground, with no distance to see across.

Fusion rather than relationship: the two drives act as one, reinforcing each other and losing the ability to operate separately. Whatever else is true of the pairing, it is not something you can be objective about, because there is no vantage point outside it.
aspects.sextile:
An opportunity that stays an opportunity until you use it.

A cooperative angle between compatible elements: the two work well together, but unlike a trine nothing happens on its own. It is the aspect most often wasted, because ease that requires initiative looks from the inside exactly like nothing at all.
aspects.square:
Two drives at right angles, each obstructing the other into growth.

The classic developmental friction: incompatible modes of operating in the same mode of action, producing crisis, effort and eventual competence. Squares are where the work is, and charts without them tend to lack the pressure that makes anyone bother.
aspects.trine:
A talent that arrived complete and was never examined.

Two drives in the same element, flowing into each other without resistance. It is genuine ability and it is unearned, which is why it is so often left unused or taken for granted; the risk of a trine is not difficulty but complacency.
aspects.quincunx:
Two parts of you with nothing in common, obliged to share a life.

No element, no mode, no shared vantage: the pairing cannot be resolved, only continually adjusted. It produces a persistent low awkwardness rather than a crisis, and it is the aspect most likely to be felt for years before it can be named.
aspects.opposition:
Two drives facing each other across the chart, each visible only in the other.

Polarity rather than conflict: what sits opposite tends to be met in other people before it is recognised as yours. Handled badly it is projection and see-saw; handled well it is the widest perspective the chart offers, because only an opposition can see both ends at once.
aspects.semisextile:
Two adjacent areas of life that share a border and little else.

Signs either side of a boundary have no element, no mode and no natural sympathy in common, so this is a connection you have to make deliberately rather than one that operates on its own. It is mild, it is easy to miss entirely, and what it asks for is translation between two parts of you that do not speak the same language.
aspects.semisquare:
A low, persistent irritation rather than a crisis.

Half a square, and it behaves like one: friction without the drama, a recurring snag that never quite escalates into something you would sit down and address. Its usefulness is that it keeps prompting action on a small scale, and its danger is that it is easy to live around for decades.
aspects.sesquiquadrate:
Friction that surfaces late, after the situation has already developed.

A square and a half, and it carries the square's demand for adjustment without its urgency. The tension tends to appear once something is well under way rather than at the outset, so it reads as a complication that arrived rather than a conflict you walked into.
aspects.quintile:
A specialised talent that runs on its own logic.

A fifth of the circle, outside the Ptolemaic family entirely, and it describes a channel between two parts of you that produces something neither would produce alone. It shows up as craft, pattern-sense or a particular knack rather than as ease or difficulty, and it is usually invisible until it is exercised.
aspects.sesquiquintile:
The same creative channel, arrived at by a longer route.

Three-tenths of the circle, in the quintile family and carrying its character: a specialised aptitude rather than a comfort or a conflict. It tends to operate at one remove, showing itself in how you approach a problem rather than in the result, and it rewards being noticed and used on purpose.
